name: Chicken and Bean Burrito

intro_html: This is the cheapest, simplest burrito in the batch, and it still turns in {{protein}} grams of protein at about {{cal}} calories on a tortilla with 18 grams of fiber. The move is a rotisserie chicken with the skin pulled off, which gives you tender pulled meat with none of the fat the skin adds. Whole black beans, salsa, a little cheese, and warm spices do the rest. When you are tired and hungry, this is the one you can build with a store chicken and a can opener.
ingredients_display: Rotisserie Chicken (generic (USDA)): 2.62 lb pulled, skin removed (1190 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Rotisserie Chicken, 2.62 lb pulled, skin removed: ~$10.15. Buy 2 whole birds: $11.94.
Mexican Cheese Blend, 7 oz: ~$1.49. Buy 1 8 oz bag: $1.73.
Pantry seasonings (ground cumin, chili powder, garlic powder): ~$0.53. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $26.34 across 14 servings, so roughly $1.88 per burrito. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $32.27 across 14 servings, roughly $2.31 per burrito. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $2.77 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $35.04. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: That is about ${{cost_ps}} a burrito (at everyday cost) versus $8 or more for a fast-food bean and chicken burrito. A rotisserie bird on a busy night is still cheaper than the drive-through.
shop_smart: A store rotisserie chicken is a deal in disguise. It is already cooked, and pulling the skin off before you shred it drops the fat without touching the protein. Buy the birds the day you cook so they are still warm and easy to pull.
Canned black beans are the budget engine here. Buy the standard 15 ounce cans, drain and rinse, and they add protein and fiber for pennies. Season them yourself so you control the salt.
Buy the block-shredded Mexican blend, not the fancy bag. A single 8 ounce bag is plenty across the batch, and the flavor difference disappears the second it melts.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Pull the skin off the rotisserie chicken and discard it, then shred the white and dark meat off the bones.
Warm the black beans in a pot with a little of their liquid, and stir in the ground cumin, chili powder, and garlic powder.
Fold the salsa into the shredded chicken so every piece is coated.
Warm the tortillas so they roll without cracking.
Spoon a layer of the spiced black beans on each tortilla, add the salsa chicken, and top with the Mexican cheese blend before you wrap.
portion_html: Set the pot of beans on your scale and subtract the empty-pot weight from Step 1, and portion the chicken the same way. Divide each by 14 so every burrito lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.

steps: Pull the skin off the rotisserie chicken and shred the meat.
Warm the black beans and stir in the cumin, chili powder, and garlic powder.
Coat the shredded chicken in the salsa.
Spread beans on warmed tortillas, add the salsa chicken, and top with the cheese.
Weigh the batch and divide into 14 equal burritos.
